items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'George Orson's song' as part of a story the interviewee does not remember; the interviewee does not confirm any personal interaction or relationship with George Orson.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. and little dad, Vincent, Turner Banja, Roy Evans on drums, Earl Hunter, myself on trombone, Lee Collins on trumpet, and with the addition of Buddy, maybe we had two trumpets for us. Yes.

And a seven-piece arch. Well, now in this story, it's slightly different from the story I've had before, because I've heard that you played with Buddy, or he played with you in George Orson's song. Then you had some kind of a, you know, Buddy didn't get on with Buddy or something, and you fired Buddy, and you got Lee Collins after Buddy left. No, I don't remember that.

You don't remember that? Oh. But I do remember playing with Buddy when he had his band just extra, when his trombone player was sick. That was quite a while ago, before he went to Manaville. He had a popular officer out there until he went down. Yeah. But before he was fine, Buddy, that didn't happen. Those buddies made up his mind he wanted to go back over to Manaville where his wife was. So, he was working over there,
